text.text: How to use it
When an event is booked, add tasks for each phase with due dates.
Review the list weekly with the client manager.
Move the event stage as phases finish.
Before you ask
Confirm date, guest count, budget and what the client cares about.
Check the vendor's rating and notes in the directory.
Booking
Request availability and a written quote for the exact scope.
Compare at least two options for the large lines.
Send the contract for the client's approval; log it as Contract sent.
Record the deposit due date and the balance date.
When signed, press Lock in and add the load-in time to the event page.
After the event
Pay the balance on time, update the rating, and add notes for next time.
A run of show is a minute-by-minute promise. Everyone should be able to read their line and know what to do.
Contents
Time, what happens, who leads, and what is needed (audio, lighting, props).
Load-in and load-out times for every vendor.
Contacts for the venue, caterer and anyone with a key.
Building it
Start from the client's must-have moments and place them first.
Work out meal service and speeches around the venue's timing rules.
Share a draft with vendors two weeks out and collect corrections.
Print copies for the planner, venue and each vendor lead.
On the day
Walk the room one hour before doors with the venue manager, then do a final check on audio, lighting and the first moment of the program.
Within three days
Thank-you notes sent to the client and key vendors
Final headcount and vendor invoices collected
Rented items counted and returned
Photos and links saved on the event page
Within two weeks
Hold a short debrief with the team: what worked, what did not, what to change.
Update vendor ratings and notes.
Ask the client for a review.
Press Wrap up on the event and move open tasks to Done or delete them.
